excerpt_text: I first noticed warmth across my chest. The situation had not changed, but my attention was no longer trapped by the worry.
interpretive_memo: Body sensation and attentional movement are narrated together.

excerpt_text: The tears came before I could explain anything. I understood them as relief and as being known by God.
interpretive_memo: Tears acquire meaning through a perceived relationship.

excerpt_text: During prayer I felt loved rather than judged. That changed the story I had been telling about myself.
interpretive_memo: Divine relationship supports a revised self-narrative.

excerpt_text: The peace was intense that evening, but what made it last was talking about it with people who knew me well.
interpretive_memo: Community is described as a mechanism of durability.

excerpt_text: I was grateful the next morning, although the old fear returned later. Recovery felt more like a rhythm than a single cure.
interpretive_memo: The account resists a simple permanent-transformation story.

excerpt_text: I could choose whether to continue the prayer and I remained able to work. That sense of control mattered to how I understood it.
interpretive_memo: Agency and functioning help describe, not diagnose, the experience.
